I am an old woman, and this small plot near the house is where I plant my maize every year with some beans and pumpkin between the rows. I cannot afford much fertilizer from the market, but I carry the droppings from my goats and chickens to the field before the rains. I keep some seed from last harvest like my mother taught me, and my children and grandchildren help me weed when school is finished. The rains from the sky are what water my maize — I have no pump, no borehole for this plot.
